mbm-2676.clue: The border is made of sleeves nobody rolled up.
mbm-2676.quote: My aunt wore her formal shirts buttoned to the wrist. I kept all the little cuff buttons along the edge of her quilt. When she folds it neatly they line up like guests at her table.

mbm-2677.clue: I left two tracks and one drawing.
mbm-2677.quote: On a gentle practice slope I skied a wide pair of loops. From the lift they looked like my sister's glasses. She made me promise to add a nose next run.

mbm-2678.clue: My shoes have the tune written underneath.
mbm-2678.quote: I painted a little spiral on the sole of each folk-dance shoe. When the floor is dusty we leave pairs of spirals. By the end of the circle the room has a song you can sweep.

mbm-2679.clue: We pack the weather with the board.
mbm-2679.quote: My aunt cut two paper clouds for her homemade travel game. Roll a six and one cloud moves over the mountains. I've spent several fine afternoons stuck in magnificent cardboard rain.

mbm-2680.clue: The last domino has a velvet bed.
mbm-2680.quote: We lost the double blank after our first porch game and found it in the cushion the next summer. I sewed a little green pouch for it. We tuck it in before we put away the rest.

mbm-2681.clue: My quilt hangs the right way up for birds.
mbm-2681.quote: I made tree shapes from my cousins' green shirts and hung the quilt on the washing line. A robin sat along the top branch. That settled which edge had to be the sky.

mbm-2682.clue: I can run from one open window to the next.
mbm-2682.quote: On Saturday mornings I follow the sound of the neighborhood piano teacher warming up. The scales go up while I run uphill and down on my return. Some Saturdays I forget to start my watch.

mbm-2683.clue: My hiking journal wears a bootlace.
mbm-2683.quote: The bootlace around my hiking journal keeps the pressed leaves inside. When my friend's lace snapped on the trail, I gave him mine. He carried the book shut with both hands all the way home.

mbm-2684.clue: The missing button comes back warm.
mbm-2684.quote: I make Dad's brass button vanish into a folded paper fan. My nephew found it behind his ear and held it tight all evening. When he gave it back it was warmer than my whole hand.

mbm-2685.clue: My stitching stops for the ferry.
mbm-2685.quote: I quilt by the harbor window. Whenever the ferry horn sounds I change thread color for three stitches. A busy afternoon leaves a little fleet of red marks down the seam.

mbm-2686.clue: My teacher gave me one floor tile to clean.
mbm-2686.quote: After my first martial arts class I scrubbed a single mat tile while the others stacked the room. I still look for my tile when I visit. It reminds me how small a beginning can be.

mbm-2687.clue: I heard a stranger laugh inside my helmet bag.
mbm-2687.quote: At the skydiving club we all brought the same canvas bag. One day I unzipped mine and found somebody's tiny squeaky duck instead of my goggles. He uses it to recognize his bag by touch. I tied a walnut to my zipper; my ears prefer it.

mbm-2688.clue: My climbing shoes stay on the floor at dinner.
mbm-2688.quote: At the wall my partner and I name each route after a meal. Last week we solved Soup and abandoned Toast halfway up. My mum thinks our climbing diary is a very strange menu.

mbm-2689.clue: I sang the highest note to a sleeping cat.
mbm-2689.quote: Our choir director told me to practice without tightening my shoulders. I sang to the cat in my lap. The instant I tensed up she'd stand and leave. She kept the whole lesson wonderfully honest.

mbm-2690.clue: The lodge has my first turn on a napkin.
mbm-2690.quote: I drew my first clean linked turns on a brown napkin at lunch. The cook pinned it above the kettle. Whenever I take the chair up I know there's a little paper track waiting at the bottom.

mbm-2691.clue: We play the last hand by lantern color.
mbm-2691.quote: My grandfather's lantern throws a yellow circle across our domino table. When the circle slips off the last tile it's time to pack up. On good nights he moves the lamp an inch.

mbm-2692.clue: All the crooked stitches lean toward home.
mbm-2692.quote: I sewed on the bus with the quilt bunched on my knees. Every bump left a little jog in a seam. My cousin can point to the patch done on the road past our house.

mbm-2693.clue: Our alley's first home crowd fit on a shelf.
mbm-2693.quote: I used to line up tiny clay spectators next to the shoes while Mum bowled. The alley owner kept them when the cafe changed hands. I found my purple gentleman cheering me on from the shoe counter twenty years later.

mbm-2694.clue: My best brush came from the kitchen.
mbm-2694.quote: I tried painting grass with a little pastry brush. It made perfect fat wildflowers instead. The baker asked for it back and got a small painting of his whole garden as interest.

mbm-2695.clue: The first peal I called smelled of apples.
mbm-2695.quote: The bell tower window looked straight down on the market. After we rang I found an apple waiting by my bicycle from the fruit seller. He said the bells had emptied his whole basket.

mbm-2696.clue: The bass drum has our old map inside.
mbm-2696.quote: Our band stuffed a creased road map in the bass drum to soften its thump. We played one more town than that map showed. I drew it in before we packed the van.

mbm-2697.clue: The back of my quilt tells on the front.
mbm-2697.quote: My mum says you learn who sewed a quilt by looking at its knots. Mine are lopsided little bows. I turned one corner back deliberately so anyone can recognize my hand.

mbm-2698.clue: I practiced for the pie contest with a spoonful of air.
mbm-2698.quote: My niece sat opposite an empty plate and counted down a practice round. Her imaginary pie was banana, mine apple. At the real fair I bought us both slices and let the timer sit.

mbm-2699.clue: The little blue whale holds my bus money.
mbm-2699.quote: I crocheted a whale for my key ring and accidentally left a gap along his back. Two coins fit inside. On wet mornings the whale pays our fare and rides in my pocket.

mbm-2700.clue: We waltz where the carpet ends.
mbm-2700.quote: My parents' living room had room for one clean ballroom turn on the bare boards by the door. At our local dance hall I still smile when I take the second turn without meeting a wall.
